beats.text: How do search, cache, and analytics learn of a change?
beats.say: How do other systems, like search, caches, and analytics, find out when your database changes?

beats.text: Polling: slow, heavy, and it misses deletes.
beats.say: One way is polling: constantly asking the database what changed. It's slow, it adds load, and it can miss deletes.

beats.text: Databases already log every change first.
beats.say: But every database already writes each change to a transaction log first, so it can recover from crashes.

beats.text: CDC reads the log and emits events, in order.
beats.say: Change data capture reads that log, and turns each change into an event, in the exact order it happened.

beats.text: Consumers update in near real time.
beats.say: Those events flow into a stream, and every consumer updates itself in near real time.

beats.text: No app changes. Captures deletes. Powers outbox relays.
beats.say: You don't change your application code, deletes are captured too, and it's the usual way to build an outbox relay.
